answer: An agent market's kernel requires every identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding for work; cryptographic proof that an agent signed conflicting commitments burns its deposit. A tide of fake accounts therefore brings no free capacity: controlling 1,000 eligible agents ties up 100,000 tokens, and using them to make conflicting commitments risks losing that stake. Even at the zenith of demand, new names cannot bypass the collateral rule.
